web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity
question: Is EQT in an actionable Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend, or is the tape signaling patience below structural resistance?

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock in Stage 4, no matter how cheap it looks on fundamentals. Wait for the trend to turn in your favor.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

web_blocks.html: While EQT's business fundamentals pass every operational KPI check, the technical tape as of November 13, 2026 urges discipline rather than haste [23]. EQT closed at $52.81 (+0.86% on the day, +3.57% on the week), sitting 22.61% below its 52-week high of $68.24 and 10.16% above its 52-week low of $47.94 [23]. Crucially, the stock remains below its primary structural moving-average floors: the 200-day SMA ($55.48, -4.81% below), the 30-week SMA ($53.47), the 40-week EMA ($53.93), and the 20-day SMA ($53.61), while hovering just $0.12 above its 50-day SMA ($52.69) [23].

web_blocks.takeaway: EQT is consolidating quietly at 0.69x volume below its 30-week and 200-day floors during a US Market Correction (6 distribution days); neither a momentum breakout nor a deep support washout is present at $52.81 [23, 24].

web_blocks.html: Our multi-timeframe check confirms the same restraint. Note that while the automated market-facts tag prints a generic 50-DMA warning under Stage 1 (Basing), EQT's $52.81 close sits +0.23% above its 50-day SMA ($52.69) while remaining below the 30-week SMA ($53.47) and 200-day SMA ($55.48) with 7 stock-level distribution days over the past 25 sessions [23]. On the 4-hour chart, EQT has nudged above its 4H 20-EMA ($52.54) with a 4H RSI of 50.79, but the 4H 50-SMA ($53.60) and daily 20-SMA ($53.61) cap upside. Meanwhile, the US market regime sits in a Correction (6 index distribution days), and options scan stamps NO_OPTIONS_EDGE ($45/$57.5 call spread costs $7.50 for $5.00 max gain, 0.67:1 R:R).

book_paragraphs: If Chapters 1 through 6 made you admire EQT's operational machine, Chapter 8 is where we step back from the geology and ask the market tape a simple, unforgiving question: do big institutional buyers agree with us right now?

At $52.81, the honest answer is: not yet. Pull up the weekly chart and look at the 30-week simple moving average—Stan Weinstein's dividing line between Stage 2 accumulation and Stage 4 distribution. EQT's 30-week SMA sits at $53.47, and its 200-day SMA sits higher at $55.48. Trading at $52.81 means EQT is still beneath both structural floors, 22.6% off its 52-week high of $68.24.

Now look at volume. On Friday, November 13, EQT traded 5.92 million shares against a 30-day average of 8.61 million—just 0.69x normal volume. When a stock stabilizes on light volume below its 200-day moving average, it tells you sellers are taking a breather, not that institutions are aggressively accumulating. Yes, the 4-hour chart shows a mild bounce above its 20-EMA ($52.54) with RSI at 50.79, and the stock closed twelve cents above its 50-day SMA ($52.69). That is a pulse, not a Stage 2 breakout.

Add the macro backdrop. The broader S&P 500 is in a Correction regime—below its 50-day moving average, carrying six distribution days in the last 25 sessions, with fewer than half of tracked stocks above their 200-day lines. And when we checked the options chain for a defined-risk call spread, the math failed: a $45/$57.5 call spread costs $7.50 for $5.00 of maximum profit—a 0.67-to-1 payoff that no disciplined trader should touch.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest skill in investing is not finding good companies—it is refusing to pay full price in the middle of a range. At $52.81, EQT is in no-man's-land: too far above the $48.00–$50.50 support shelf for a deep-value entry, and still below the $55.48 200-day floor for a momentum breakout.

book_subsections.title: Two Clean Technical Triggers: Support Shelf vs. Stage 2 Reclaim
paragraphs: Because we respect both value and trend, we map two distinct, rule-based triggers. The first is the Support Shelf Entry ($48.00–$50.50), anchored by Pivot S1 ($49.94) and the 52-week low ($47.94), backed by a hard invalidation stop at $44.50 (just above Pivot S2 at $44.49). Entering in that zone gives us 2.25-to-1 reward-to-risk to our $64.00 base target.

The second is the Stage 2 Reclaim Trigger ($55.50+). If EQT powers back above its 30-week SMA ($53.47) and 200-day SMA ($55.48) on at least 1.3x 30-day average volume—likely catalyzed by a cold December forecast or early HSR clearance on the Range merger—then trend-following institutions will be forced to cover shorts and chase. Until one of those two doors opens, patience costs nothing.

book_subsections.title: Institutional Ownership, Short Interest & Options Desk Audit
paragraphs: Look beneath the price bars at who owns the float. Institutional ownership sits at 97.57% with a +1.49% positive institutional transaction tilt, while short interest is a modest 3.93% of float (24.35 million shares, or 3.10 days to cover). That 3.93% short float is largely merger-arbitrage hedging against Range Resources rather than an aggressive fundamental short attack—which means once the Range deal closes in Q1 2027, that mechanical short pressure vanishes.

Even so, options pricing refuses to subsidize an early entry. With daily ATR at $1.69 and Bollinger Band width at 14.77%, implied volatility is too rich relative to realized movement for bull call spreads to clear our 1.25:1 payoff floor. When both the weekly trend and the options math say 'stand aside,' you listen.

book_subsections.title: Reading Market Regime & Breadth Before Pulling the Trigger
paragraphs: Even the cleanest single-stock setup struggles when the broader market tape is distributing shares. With the S&P 500 sitting in a Correction regime—below its 50-day moving average, carrying six distribution days in the past 25 sessions, and showing only 47.4% of tracked stocks above their 200-day lines—breakouts fail far more often than they follow through.

In a Correction regime, disciplined capital demands either a clear Stage 2 relative-strength leader or a deep pullback into a pre-defined support shelf where weak hands have already capitulated. EQT at $52.81 offers neither right now, which is precisely why our playbook waits for $48.00–$50.50 or a confirmed $55.50+ volume reclaim.

book_subsections.title: Volume, Volatility & Moving-Average Discipline
paragraphs: Notice how cleanly moving averages act as an institutional lie detector. When big pension funds and sovereign wealth desks are quietly accumulating a $33 billion energy major, the stock holds above its 30-week and 200-day moving averages and expands on up-week volume. Today, EQT sits below both long-term averages on 0.69x normal volume.

Respecting the tape does not mean ignoring fundamentals; it means refusing to fight institutional distribution or merger-arbitrage supply until either price reaches a high-conviction support shelf ($48.00–$50.50) or buyers prove their conviction by reclaiming $55.50 on heavy volume.
